\hypertarget{doc-brownfield-import}{%
\chapter{Export existing configuration and translate it into Terraform}\label{doc-brownfield-import}}

\texttt{watchover\ export} reads what already exists in an Akeyless account and translates it into
Terraform. It only \textbf{reads}: nothing in Akeyless changes until you apply.

Not exported: secret values, keys, rotated/dynamic secret definitions, event forwarders (no list
operation).

\hypertarget{transport-cli-or-rest}{%
\section{Transport: CLI or REST}\label{transport-cli-or-rest}}

\texttt{-\/-transport\ cli} (default) runs the \texttt{akeyless} CLI with \texttt{-\/-profile} (SSO logins work).
\texttt{-\/-transport\ api} calls the REST API directly with \texttt{-\/-token} / \texttt{\$AKEYLESS\_TOKEN}, with no binary
needed. Both read the same operations and produce identical output (tested). See
\protect\hyperlink{doc-api-vs-cli}{api-vs-cli.md}. Gateway reads need \texttt{-\/-gateway-url\ https://gw:8000} (CLI) or
\texttt{-\/-gateway-api\ https://gw:8000/api/v2} (REST).

The auth-method field mapping (e.g. Azure \texttt{bound\_service\_principal\_ids} -\textgreater{} \texttt{bound\_spid}, AWS
\texttt{account\_id} -\textgreater{} \texttt{bound\_aws\_account\_id}) was taken from the provider 2.0.5 read code of every
\texttt{akeyless\_auth\_method\_*} resource.

\hypertarget{two-modes}{%
\section{Two modes}\label{two-modes}}

\textbf{Model mode (default)}: for this repository\textquotesingle s data-driven Terraform.

\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize,breaklines,breakanywhere,frame=leftline,framerule=1.2pt,rulecolor=\color{wo-rule},xleftmargin=6pt]
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --profile admin \
  --exclude '^/governance/roles/platform/terraform-' --exclude '^/governance/auth/ci-terraform$'
\end{Verbatim}

Writes \texttt{model/roles/imported.yaml}, \texttt{model/auth\_methods.imported.yaml}, \texttt{model/folders.imported.yaml},
\texttt{model/governance.imported.yaml} and \texttt{imports.tf} with the \texttt{for\_each} addresses of \texttt{terraform/*.tf}.

\textbf{HCL mode}: plain Terraform written by Terraform itself, for anything, including PKI issuers,
account settings and auth-method types the YAML model doesn\textquotesingle t cover.

\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize,breaklines,breakanywhere,frame=leftline,framerule=1.2pt,rulecolor=\color{wo-rule},xleftmargin=6pt]
export AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID=p-... AKEYLESS_ACCESS_KEY=...       # read-only identity; provider env login
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --profile admin --hcl --generate
\end{Verbatim}

Writes \texttt{hcl/providers.tf} and \texttt{hcl/imports.tf} (one flat import block per object). With
\texttt{-\/-generate} it then runs \texttt{terraform\ init} and \texttt{terraform\ plan\ -generate-config-out=generated.tf}:
the provider reads every object and Terraform writes its \texttt{resource} blocks into
\texttt{hcl/generated.tf}. Without \texttt{-\/-generate}, run those two commands yourself in \texttt{hcl/}.

The persona view uses the same sub-claim rules as the simulator (OR within a key, AND across keys,
globs, case sensitivity per association). An auth method is configured per identity provider,
not per user: "the OIDC config for a user" is the OIDC auth method plus the associations whose
sub-claims match that user\textquotesingle s claims.

\hypertarget{secrets}{%
\section{Secrets}\label{secrets}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Exported files never contain secrets. In \texttt{raw/}, \texttt{client\_secret}, access keys, passwords,
  private keys and tokens are replaced with \texttt{\textless{}redacted\textgreater{}}.
\item
  OIDC auth methods get a \texttt{client\_secret\_var}, which you fill in \texttt{TF\_VAR\_auth\_method\_secrets}.
\item
  In \texttt{generated.tf}, Terraform can\textquotesingle t read back sensitive values. Replace those with variables
  before applying.
\item
  After import, the state holds what the provider reads (e.g. API-key access keys). Treat the
  state as secret.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{procedure}{%
\section{Procedure}\label{procedure}}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Run the export and read \texttt{REPORT.md}. It lists everything that needs a decision: temporary rules
  (skipped), unknown rule types, root-scope roles, unsupported auth-method types, associations to
  objects outside the export, OIDC secrets to provide, issuers and settings that need \texttt{-\/-hcl}.
\item
  Model mode: move the files into \texttt{terraform/model/} (merge with existing files, drop \texttt{.imported})
  and copy \texttt{imports.tf} into \texttt{terraform/}. HCL mode: review \texttt{generated.tf}, then either keep the
  plain resources in their own state, or move them into the YAML model.
\item
  Run \texttt{terraform\ plan} until it shows \textbf{only imports}, with no create, destroy or replace. Then apply.
\item
  Delete \texttt{imports.tf}.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{VERIFY}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  How \texttt{list-items} reports nested folders. The walk is breadth-first and bounded by \texttt{-\/-max-depth}.
\item
  Which \texttt{item\_type} the API uses for PKI issuers. An item counts as an issuer when it has
  \texttt{pki\_cert\_issuer\_details}, or when its type contains both PKI and ISSUER. \texttt{REPORT.md} lists
  the item types seen.
\item
  That \texttt{import} blocks can\textquotesingle t be exercised against a mocked provider (an OpenTofu limitation):
  in this repository they are validated, and their model plans are tested without them.
\end{itemize}
